#3238 · do user-typed fork-skill invocations background?

Two sessions carried this as an unverified caveat. Transcript archaeology settles it.

✅ VERDICT: YES. User-typed invocations background by default on CC ≥ 2.1.218, and background: false restores foreground on the exact same path. The 23 /ork: commands were live-degraded until #3093's declarations shipped.

Leg 1 no opt-out → BACKGROUND

CC 2.1.218 (07-23, 07-24) and 2.1.220 (07-26, 07-29). Skill versions at those timestamps had no background: false.

{"type":"system","subtype":"local_command",
 "content":"<local-command-stdout>Running in the
   background as @hq-ext-handoff</local-command-stdout>
 <forked-skill-launch>{"skillName":"hq-ext:handoff",...}",
 "version":"2.1.218"}

Leg 2 background: false → FOREGROUND

CC 2.1.220, 2026-08-01 16:47. Same skill, same typed path, hq-ext 1.38.1 (first version declaring the opt-out).

16:47:41 user   /hq-ext:handoff all ...
16:51:29 system/local_command
  <local-command-stdout>All three legs are
  resolved...</local-command-stdout>
# ~4 min blocking; result IS the command stdout.
# Zero forked-skill-launch, zero task-notification.

Observed timeline

2026-07-23 → 07-29 08:44 4 sessions: typed handoff backgroundsdegraded
2026-07-29 18:11 hq-ext 1.38.1 installed: first background: false
2026-08-01 16:47 typed handoff runs foreground, receipt inlinerestored
2026-08-01 (#3239 → v9.4.x) all 23 /ork: user-invocable fork skills declare the opt-outfixed
Why the two "pre-2.1.218 counterexamples" dissolved

Two sessions whose first recorded version was 2.1.215 / 2.1.217 also contained backgrounded records — but each record's own envelope said "version":"2.1.218": the sessions upgraded mid-flight. Every genuine backgrounded record sits on ≥ 2.1.218, and every one predates the first background: false install. Bonus lesson: the probe scripts themselves contaminated later greps (this session's transcript contains the search strings), so every match was verified by record envelope, not by substring.
